I reproduced this through the SDK: **$2,604.33/month**, with the tax-free threshold claimed, produces **$208 withholding instead of $212**. This affects the shared pay rule used by the SDK and API calculators. Add the adjustment and a regression test for this example. [Official Schedule 1](https://www.legislation.gov.au/F2025L01016/asmade/2025-09-01/text/original/epub/OEBPS/document_1/document_1.html).

2. **[P1] Select student-loan coefficients using the tax-free-threshold answer** — [stsl-component.ts:72](/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/packages/rules/au/stsl/src/rules/stsl-component.ts:72)

   The student-loan rule never reads `TaxFreeThresholdClaimedFact`; its table contains only the coefficients for claiming the threshold. The surrounding rule pack accepts either answer. Using Schedule 8’s own example—**$10,627.88/month without claiming the threshold**—TaxKit returns **$763 student-loan withholding instead of $1,018**, a $255 shortfall. This affects the student-loan rule packs exposed through `taxkit/au`. Add the missing table selection and tests for both answers. [Official Schedule 8, example 3](https://www.legislation.gov.au/F2025L01016/asmade/2025-09-01/text/original/epub/OEBPS/document_1/document_1.html).

3. **[P2] Record the student-loan ledger’s actual rule identity** — [withholdings-ledger.ts:59](/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/packages/rules/au/pay/src/rules/withholdings-ledger.ts:59)

   The shared ledger builder always records `PayWithholdingsLedgerRuleId`, including when called by the student-loan aggregator. That calculation’s declared rule is `PayWithholdingsLedgerWithStslRuleId`. An in-memory calculation confirmed that the explanation names a rule absent from its selected rule graph. Amounts are unaffected, but matching the explanation back to the rule definitions fails. Pass the owning rule identity into the builder and correct the test that currently expects the wrong identity.
